topIssues.title: op-supernode: logsDB does not recover from reorgs that occur while supernode is offline
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
**Claude:** Filed on behalf of @ajsutton.

## Problem

If an L2 reorg invalidates a sealed block in op-supernode's per-chain `logs.db` while supernode is stopped, supernode cannot recover on restart and gets stuck in an infinite retry loop.

## Mechanism

On restart, `backfillChain` (`op-supernode/supernode/activity/interop/log_backfill.go:113-140`) trusts the persisted `LatestSealedBlock` and resumes from `latest.Number + 1`:

```go
if latest, has := db.LatestSealedBlock(); has { startNum = latest.Number + 1 }
```

If the canonical chain no longer extends what's stored, the next seal trips `ErrParentHashMismatch` or `ErrStaleLogsDB` in `sealBlockDataIntoLogsDB` (`logdb.go:139-160`). `Start` (`interop.go:287-305`) catches the error and retries backfill on a fixed backoff with no rewind, indefinitely.

The online rewind path (`DecisionRewind` → `applyRewindPlan`, `interop.go:760-872`) — which can `Clear()` or `Rewind()` logsDBs — is gated behind reaching the main algorithm loop, which backfill blocks. So it never fires for this case.

## Impact

Operator must manually delete the affected chain's `logs.db` to recover. This also covers the activation-block reorg case (a reorg that invalidates the first sealed block).

## Suggested direction

On `ErrParentHashMismatch` / `ErrStaleLogsDB` during backfill, trim the logsDB back to the latest block whose hash still matches the canonical chain (or `Clear()` if no such block exists, i.e. the activation block itself was reorged) and retry, rather than spinning on the same failing seal.

topPRs.title: fix(op-supernode): recover logsDB from offline L2 reorg on restart
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
Closes ethereum-optimism/optimism#20627.

If an L2 reorg invalidated a sealed block in a chain's `logs.db` while supernode was stopped, `backfillChain` resumed from `LatestSealedBlock+1` and tripped `ErrParentHashMismatch` on the first seal forever — the only operator recovery was deleting `logs.db`. The online rewind path was unreachable because it's gated behind the main loop, which backfill blocks.

Fix: before resuming, `reconcileLogsDBTail` walks back through the sealed range to find the deepest block still on canonical, then `Rewind`s once (or `Clear`s if no sealed block matches). Single pass, single truncation regardless of reorg depth. No-reorg cost is one extra `OutputV0AtBlockNumber` per chain per restart.

topPRs.title: fix(op-wheel): route logs to stderr to keep stdout JSON clean
topPRs.author: Theburaka
topPRs.body:
The global log handler in `op-wheel` was wired to `os.Stdout`, so any log line interleaved with the JSON emitted by `cheat head-block`, `cheat head-header`, and `engine status` (all via `ctx.App.Writer`). Switched to `os.Stderr`, matching `op-chain-ops/cmd/check-derivation`, so `jq` and friends can parse the output.

- [x] `go build ./...` in `op-wheel`
- [ ] manual: `op-wheel cheat head-block ... | jq .`
